claims.statement: The Linux host's Chromium 155 headless surface (loopback CDP, throwaway profile, throwaway HOME/XDG, --disable-extensions) now carries the KEY-EVENT DELIVERY-BOUNDARY measurement for CapsLock - the r57 planned residual executed and honestly closed as a MEASURED NEGATIVE on the latch - capability chromium-keyevent-delivery-boundary-linux: the CapsLock leg (key CapsLock, code CapsLock, windowsVirtualKeyCode 20, no text; keyDown+keyUp, TWICE) delivers events the page records with the full delivered shape (key, code, keyCode 20, cancelable true, defaultPrevented false), while getModifierState('CapsLock') reads FALSE on EVERY recorded event - down, up, and the subsequent nonce letters (the page's recorder records getModifierState('CapsLock') on every keydown/keyup). The measured boundary: CDP Input.dispatchKeyEvent cannot set Blink's caps-lock state bit on this surface - the CDP modifier mapping carries only bits 1/2/4/8 (S162: GetEventModifiers in content/browser/devtools/protocol/input_handler.cc) while getModifierState('CapsLock') tests Blink's kCapsLockOn = 1<<9 (third_party/blink WebInputEvent key-state table); the boundary is measured from BOTH sides - delivered-shape witnesses (the events DO deliver) and the persistent absence witness (the latch flag does NOT set) - with the live probe receipt .ufo/waves/round-59/runner/probe-capslock.json (probe script under the runner seat's scratch, receipt committed). This separates 'event delivered but state not settable over CDP' from 'event not delivered' - the knowledge the r57 planned residual was after. The ROUTED D4 positive control rides the same generation: a second form page /form2 (same fixture shape, no swallower) where the same Ctrl+Enter chord DOES submit - exactly one /echo2 request, witnessed client-side and server-side. The r59 counter generation implements the ROUTED D1 page-vs-block cross-check (every swallow-block entry (key, cancelable, defaultPrevented) matched BY VALUE against journey.form.pageKeylog; mismatch -> finding keylog-flag-mismatch), the ROUTED D2 step-plan check (the receipt's recorded steps must equal the declared 18-step list; mismatch -> finding step-plan-mismatch), and the CapsLock boundary checks (delivered shape on every CapsLock/letter event; capsLatchExpected false asserted against the receipt's named expectation; any true is a finding). killRules.C2: The claim dies if the counter is green on anything but the committed receipt (synthetic-green; the D2 step-plan check and the D1 page-vs-block cross-check are the implementing checks - a forged-but-consistent receipt that still greens is a kill); the driver sha does not match the freeze pin; a CapsLock or swallow witness rests on driver-side state instead of page/server state (a forged page keylog must trip the D1 cross-check); the keylog does not record getModifierState('CapsLock') on every recorded keydown/keyup; any CapsLock or letter event lacks a delivered-shape field (key, code, keyCode, cancelable); the caps flag reads true ANYWHERE in the keylog without the counter treating it as a finding (an unexplained true means forged page state or an unmodeled surface change - either kills); more than one submission reaches either form's endpoint (exactly one /echo AND exactly one /echo2); or the D4 positive control is absent (form2's Ctrl+Enter must submit).
